Convert a group-by-individual matrix to bisonR format

Source: R/utils.R
convert_gbi_to_bison.Rd

Group-by-individual (GBI) data record which individuals were seen together in each group or sampling event, as a matrix with one row per group and one column per individual. Use this function to prepare such data for bison_model(). It produces one row for each group and each pair of individuals where at least one of the pair was present. The event column is 1 if both were present and 0 if only one was. Groups where neither individual was seen carry no information about the pair and are left out.

Usage

convert_gbi_to_bison(
  gbi,
  group_properties = NULL,
  individual_properties = NULL,
  individual_constraints = NULL
)

Arguments

gbi

A matrix with R rows (groups) and C columns (individuals) of 0s and 1s. If it has column names they are used as node names; otherwise nodes are numbered 1:C.

group_properties

Optional vector of length R with a property of each group (e.g. location), added as column group_property.

individual_properties

Optional vector of length C with a property of each individual, added as columns node_1_property and node_2_property.

individual_constraints

Optional vector of length C. Only pairs of individuals with the same value are included (for example, individuals that could have been seen together because they were in the study area at the same time).

Value

A data frame with columns node_1, node_2, event and group_id, plus any property columns, ready for use with a binary bison_model() with an effort of 1, e.g. (event | 1) ~ dyad(node_1, node_2).

See also

bison_model()

Examples

gbi <- matrix(rbinom(20 * 5, 1, 0.4), 20, 5, dimnames = list(NULL, LETTERS[1:5]))
df <- convert_gbi_to_bison(gbi)
head(df)
#>   node_1 node_2 event group_id
#> 1      A      B     0        4
#> 2      A      B     1        5
#> 3      A      B     0        6
#> 4      A      B     0        8
#> 5      A      B     0        9
#> 6      A      B     0       11
